metadata.title: Huntress: SMB/MSP managed detection, 24/7 SOC, owned EDR stack

entities.name: Huntress
entities.notes: Managed security platform for SMBs and MSPs: owned Managed EDR + Managed ITDR (Microsoft 365 identities) + Managed SIEM + SAT, operated by a 24/7 human-led SOC. CVE Numbering Authority. Distinct from CrowdStrike-class enterprise EDR sold as a console; Huntress sells the SOC as the product. Vendor-claimed scale (endpoints/identities) is not independently audited here.

entities.name: Huntress_SOC
entities.notes: 24/7 SOC wrapping Huntress telemetry. Why it works for SMBs: detection-to-remediation is staffed, so a shop without a SOC still gets a human on the incident. Failure mode is the same as any EDR-backed SOC: if the agent is killed (BYOVD/EDR-killer) or identity is reset via helpdesk, the SOC sees a hole, not a guarantee.

entities.name: Managed_ITDR
entities.notes: Identity threat detection and response on Microsoft 365. Adjacent to helpdesk-vishing (Scattered Spider): it can see anomalous identity use after the fact; it does not replace phishing-resistant MFA or a helpdesk that will not reset on a phone call.

entities.name: MSP_Channel
entities.notes: Outsourced IT / MSP channel. Huntress's primary distribution is through MSPs protecting many small tenants, not Fortune-500 SOC buy. That is a different concentration: one MSP compromise or one bad tenant config fans out.
